title: Business Management (BUM151) MODULE
summary: Studied Business Management concepts including value chains, functional areas, organizational environments, entrepreneurship, operations and logistics, marketing strategy, financial management, HR management, and e-business/e-management/e-ethics.
details: Subject outcomes included defining value chain; listing functional areas; explaining needs in the business cycle; describing the free market system and need satisfaction institutions; explaining the organization as a system with value-adding elements; adding competitive value to a business; explaining the environment of the organization (international, macro, market, micro); and applying entrepreneurial concepts (characteristics/motivation, routes, entrepreneurial process, stages of business growth, and business ownership forms with/without legal personality). Students also covered contractual and statutory establishment requirements, location and premises layout, management skills and roles, planning and organizing concepts, organizational design, leadership principles, and types of control. Functional management topics included managerial decision-making, competitive advantage, purchasing objectives and purchasing cycle, transport modes, warehousing uses, inventory management and costs, production/operations management tasks, production layouts, quality control development, production/operations aids, outbound logistics, research and development, marketing concepts and orientations, customer service, and customer needs. Financial management topics included financial measurement/reporting, performance analysis scope, interrelationship of financial management in the organization/value chain context, budget planning and control, asset and working capital management, and income appropriation. Human resources covered HR planning/provision and retention, governance affecting HRM, and e-business/e-management, e-information evaluation, e-ethical technology trends, plus e-management challenges and opportunities. Skills emphasized illustrating and analyzing the value chain, comparing environments, applying the entrepreneurial process, applying planning/organizing/control and managerial decision-making, evaluating purchasing and marketing orientations, and assessing HR provision and e-business categories.
